items.summary: Shrek 2 Remastered is real, and its release date is less than a month away.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/19/shrek-2-remastered-1792451754506.png
Shrek 2 Remastered is real, and its release date is less than a month away.

As revealed during today's ID@Xbox showcase for October 2026, Aspyr Media has recreated a cult classic tie-in game from the original Xbox era for 2026. Shrek 2 Remastered is a modern version of Activision's co-op video game that will allow players to relive swampy memories when it comes to Xbox Series X/S next month, November 10.

The reveal trailer offers a sneak peek at how fan-favorite playable characters and classic moments from DreamWorks' fairytale sequel have been upgraded with improved graphics, new features, and more. It's been a while since players were able to play as Shrek, Fiona, Donkey, Gingy, and more, but you can get a taste of some of what's in store in the footage below.

You may have noticed that the opening isn't something from the original Shrek 2. Aspyr took today's announcement trailer as an opportunity to acknowledge the elephant in the room: That its November release date puts it within spitting distance of Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6 . Set for release just nine days later, November 19, GTA 6 seems to have convinced most other games to steer clear of its launch window – but not Shrek.

Instead of shooting for a different date, Shrek 2 Remastered is sticking to its November 10 plan. The trailer takes a tongue-in-cheek jab at Rockstar's latest, going as far as to not only recreate its Vice City vibe but even come up with its own version of that iconic Grand Theft Auto box art, too.

The original Shrek 2 video game , meanwhile, launched in 2004 and came to the GameCube, PlayStation 2, and original Xbox. While we wait for the remaster to launch in just a few short weeks, you can check out a summary for the original experience below:

"Go beyond the film as you guide Shrek and all his pals on a thrilling, squad-based action-adventure for four players. Voyage through familiar haunts like Shrek's swamp. Tag-team baddies and use each character's special abilities to solve puzzles and accomplish mission objectives."

Pre-orders for players looking to get the jump on Shrek 2 Remastered are available now. IGN's team-up with Xbox for this year's fall presentation is finally here, so be sure to keep checking in for all of the latest updates. For more, you can see everything announced during the show's April installment .

items.title: 《北极蛋》、《漱口水》和《不，我不是人类》即将登陆 Xbox | IDX盒
items.summary: Three indie games that achieved viral status over the last three years are making their long-awaited debut on

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2024/12/13/mouthwashing-blogroll-1734122174372.jpg
Three indie games that achieved viral status over the last three years are making their long-awaited debut on Xbox from publisher Critical Reflex.
As revealed during today's ID@Xbox showcase for October 2026, celebrated indie titles Arctic Eggs, Mouthwashing, and No, I'm Not a Human are making their way to Xbox for the very first time.

Physics-focused game Arctic Eggs tasks players with cooking eggs in — you guessed it — the Arctic. It sounds easy enough, but the game’s physics make this chore a true test of patience. And it’s not just eggs you’ll have to cook, either; you’ll pan fry anything from cockroaches to shot glasses, sausages, stingrays, and more, with the aim of feeding the city’s hungry inhabitants and possibly earning an audience with the Saint of Six Stomachs. Arctic Eggs, from developer The Water Museum, is available today (October 20, 2026) on Xbox Series X/S.

No, I’m Not a Human is an unsettling tale that follows a homeowner in an increasingly uninhabitable world. Players must decide who to shelter and who to turn away as the days grow hotter, with mysterious beings crawling out of the ground — beings that look, and sometimes behave, like humans. Pick the real people and wait out the apocalypse together; pick impostors and risk your housemates’ lives. No, I'm Not a Human will be available on Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, and Xbox Game Pass in 2027.

Cult indie horror game Mouthwashing , first released in September 2024, is an exciting addition to the Xbox family. Set on a shipwrecked space freighter, players are responsible for managing its remaining crew as they slowly descend into madness and self-destruction. Mouthwashing is coming to Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, and Xbox Game Pass on October 29, 2026.

IGN gave Mouthwashing a glowing review, scoring it a sparkling 9 out of 10. Reviewer Ronny Barrier praised it as a "grimy, uncomfortable, and incredibly compelling, painting an unsettling picture of who we can be in our worst moments – and it doesn’t let us get away with it."
That’s not all; Critical Reflex will be sharing more information on its YouTube channel later today.

Critical Reflex is known for a bevy of strange and interesting games that often go viral on YouTube; they've published titles like Militsioner, where players must make their escape from a giant policeman who's watching their every move, and Buckshot Roulette , where, well... you play Russian Roulette with a shotgun, with a few additional mechanics mixed in.

items.title: 和宫崎英高畅聊，寻找“类魂”游戏的魂
items.summary: 动作游戏与难度之间的关系一直十分复杂。 几十年前，古早动作游戏往往难度极高，但这并非总是设计师有意为之。它们之所以难度曲线陡峭，存在大量需要玩家反复试错的关卡或场景，很大程度上是因为在那个年代，开创动作品类的开发者们试图

content.v: 动作游戏与难度之间的关系一直十分复杂。
几十年前，古早动作游戏往往难度极高，但这并非总是设计师有意为之。它们之所以难度曲线陡峭，存在大量需要玩家反复试错的关卡或场景，很大程度上是因为在那个年代，开创动作品类的开发者们试图在确保公平性的同时，尽可能考验玩家的精准操作。在游戏行业诞生初期，这是前辈们摸索出来的最佳实践。
随着电影化叙事手法的兴起，许多动作游戏为了呈现引人入胜的剧情而降低难度，使更广泛的玩家群体能够轻松体验。从上世纪90年代末到2010年代中期，玩家可以毫不费力地通关那些游戏，几乎不会遇到任何棘手挑战。与此同时，“忍者龙剑传”系列、《超级肉肉哥》等游戏仍然为追求极致挑战的玩家提供了紧张刺激的体验。
2009年，动作游戏品类迎来了一部具有里程碑意义的作品：一款事先没有任何预热的日本高难度动作游戏横空出世，迅速吸引了众多动作游戏爱好者，并最终成为了历史上最具影响力的电子游戏之一。
http://img.chuapp.com/wp-content/Picture/2026-10-20/3536ad7393054010.jpg?imageView2/2/w/700
■ 低调大师

笔者永远不会忘记几年前与宫崎英高初次见面时的情形。2018年EA游戏展的一天，我预约了对FromSoftware另一名员工的采访，想请对方聊聊工作室正在开发的一款游戏。然而，当我推开采访室的门，却意外地见到了FromSoftware社长宫崎英高——当时我感到特别意外，完全不知道接下来会发生什么。这位曾经打造数款高难度游戏的大师，是否会在我毫无准备的情况下，给我带来一场像他的游戏那样充满挑战的考验？
幸运的是，情况并非如此。宫崎英高平易近人、不摆架子，还喜欢开玩笑活跃气氛。我对那次采访很满意，但我也希望有朝一日能再次与宫崎英高见面，畅谈他亲手开创的动作游戏细分品类：类魂（Soulslike）。如今，我终于得到了机会。

在FromSoftware位于日本东京的总部，我在一间光线灰暗的“艾尔登法环”主题房间对宫崎英高进行采访。我的准备比上次充分得多，内心却依然有些忐忑。宫崎英高面带微笑与我握手，并表示他很期待与我交谈。当我们坐下后，我告诉他，我并不打算和他聊《艾尔登法环》的细节。我想跟宫崎英高深入探讨另一个话题：在类魂游戏的诞生、发展和演变历程中，他究竟扮演了怎样的角色？听到这话，宫崎英高顿时来了精神。随着采访的进行，宫崎英高显然很享受这次交流，与我的对话甚至超出了原定采访时间。宫崎英高毫无保留地表达了对类魂游戏的浓厚兴趣和热情，但他强调，他从来不以类魂品类的发明者自居。
“我并不认为我们发明了所谓的‘类魂’品类。”宫崎英高说，“我知道很多人将我们视为品类开创者，但就游戏设计而言，对于将死亡和学习融入核心玩法循环的理念，某些玩家或许非常愿意接受，只不过以前很难找到一款像这样的游戏。”
http://img.chuapp.com/wp-content/Picture/2026-10-20/4956ad739718a8cf.jpg?imageView2/2/w/700
■ 品类鼻祖

宫崎英高于2004年加入FromSoftware，担任“装甲核心”系列游戏的程序员、设计师和总监。几年后，宫崎英高听说FromSoftware正在与索尼合作，开发一款以高难度为重点的奇幻动作游戏，并立即产生了兴趣。当时，那款游戏的开发因种种原因屡遭挫折，而宫崎英高向领导层主动请缨，请求为项目掌舵。鉴于该项目几乎毫无进展，FromSoftware认为将它交给一名入行不久、经验不足的开发者风险较低，还能达到锻炼新人的目的，于是同意了他的请求。

接手项目后，宫崎英高从FromSoftware旗下动作RPG游戏“国王密令”（King’s Field）系列中吸取灵感，同时有意识地加大游戏难度和挑战性，目的是玩家提供与经典硬核奇幻动作角色扮演游戏类似的体验。此外，他还希望充分利用现代技术，使玩家能够进行非强制的联机合作，或者仔细权衡风险和回报——这与角色死亡后玩家的行为有着直接关系。经过团队内部集思广益，宫崎英高迎来了灵感迸发的时刻，而多年以后，他最初的灵感对整个游戏行业都产生了深远影响。
宫崎英高的团队在游戏中引入了一套“魂”系统，允许玩家在角色死亡后找回掉落的升级资源，从而创造了一种关于生命、死亡和重生的全新互动方式。“我们很快发现，将死亡作为核心玩法循环的一部分是可行的，并且这个概念也能被玩家们接受。”宫崎英高解释，“但我并不觉得这是什么全新发明。我的想法是，FromSoftware的基因加上我们的设计理念，恰好满足了一些玩家的潜在需求。”
http://img.chuapp.com/wp-content/Picture/2026-10-20/6836ad739943f3c0.jpg?imageView2/2/w/700
2008年10月初，《恶魔之魂》在日本游戏杂志《Fami通》上首次公开。短短4个月后，《恶魔之魂》于2009年2月登陆PS3平台，发售前几乎没有经过任何预热宣传。这款第三人称动作RPG游戏要求玩家注重操作的精准度，辨别敌人的行动规律，并从错误中学习。当然，《恶魔之魂》更以极高的难度而闻名。

“我们经常因为游戏难度高受到赞誉，但我们并非简单地提高难度，还要做到公平合理。”宫崎英高说，“我们希望当玩家死亡时，他们能明白自己为何被杀死，并且觉得合情合理。这就是我们试图为玩家提供的游戏体验。我知道，许多玩家很可能不认同我的观点，他们会抱怨：‘你在说什么？这游戏完全不讲道理！太离谱了！’但无论如何，我们努力确保游戏里存在一条学习曲线和某种反馈循环，使玩家能够不断总结经验，吸取教训，然后再次尝试。我们相信游戏应该有难度，但我们不会制作难度不合理或不公平的游戏。”
高难度Boss战是类魂游戏的标志性特征之一，然而在发行商索尼组织的内部测试，以及在2008年东京电玩展上提供的现场试玩中，《恶魔之魂》的Boss战却未能引起积极反响。这导致索尼对《恶魔之魂》的信心受挫。雪上加霜的是，《恶魔之魂》在开发后期优化不佳，而索尼最终决定放弃投入本地化资源，不再面向欧美市场推出这款游戏。
2012年，时任索尼全球工作室总裁的吉田修平承认，他为索尼当初的决定感到后悔。“我们低估了游戏质量，日本媒体也犯了同样的错误。”吉田修平表示，“从发行角度来看，我们在工作室管理等方面犯了严重错误，当时没能意识到我们正在制作的产品的价值。”
http://img.chuapp.com/wp-content/Picture/2026-10-20/4636ad73a13bd23f.jpg?imageView2/2/w/700

Atlus接手了《恶魔之魂》在北美的发行工作（2009年10月发售），万代南梦宫则负这款游戏在欧洲地区的发行（2010年6月）。自从登陆北美市场后，《恶魔之魂》在全球范围内迅速赢得广泛好评，在游戏评测聚合网站Metacritic上的媒体平均评分达到了89分。尽管《恶魔之魂》在日本发售初期销售表现疲软，但在良好口碑效应的推动下，这款游戏的全球销量飙升，不仅促使Atlus利润大涨，还赢得了索尼“Greatest Hits”的称号（这个称号被用于标识销量达到指定目标，并降价再次发布的游戏——译注）。

2009年底，在美国，《恶魔之魂》已经成为一部备受赞誉的游戏作品，并在核心玩家圈层吸引了众多拥趸。《恶魔之魂》在商业和口碑层面的成功激励了宫崎英高，使他进一步坚定了自己的创作理念。“每当我们推出一款游戏，工作室都会收到一些反馈。我认为，《恶魔之魂》的发布极大地增强了我们的自信心，让我们决定将它的某些特质延续到《黑暗之魂》中，并不断探索和拓展新的边界。”宫崎英高说，“根据玩家反馈，我们意识到，我们所做的事情基本上符合玩家们的期待。因此，我们有勇气做出重大决策，创作拥有鲜明风格的作品。”
随着《恶魔之魂》成功地将向PlayStation玩家展现了宫崎英高游戏的独特魅力，FromSoftware开始筹备新项目，并希望工作室的下一款游戏能够产生更大影响力。为此，FromSoftware决定与《恶魔之魂》的欧洲发行商万代南梦宫合作，将新作带给更广泛的受众：多平台游戏玩家。
http://img.chuapp.com/wp-content/Picture/2026-10-20/9546ad73aa358326.jpg?imageView2/2/w/700
■ 黑魂诞生
FromSoftware希望为Xbox和PC玩家打造《恶魔之魂》续作，但由于“恶魔之魂”的IP属于索尼，宫崎英高只能重新构建一个全新黑暗奇幻世界，并在此基础上开发一款面向PS3、Xbox 360和PC平台发布的精神续作。
在《黑暗之魂》开发期间，通过采用一种自由的创作流程，宫崎英高鼓励团队成员大胆发挥，分享各自的想法和建议，并从希腊、日本和北欧等不同文化的神话中汲取灵感。初代《黑暗之魂》引入了魂系游戏标志性的篝火存档点，也进一步推动了类魂这一细分品类的发展。
作为项目总监，宫崎英高充分运用他在《恶魔之魂》开发期间积累的经验，将各种抽象概念与实际玩法相结合，完成了一部全面超越《恶魔之魂》的作品。“在总监岗位上，我做游戏的方法有点像制作三明治：我总是从非常高的概念层面出发，描绘出自己想要实现的愿景，然后再深入底层，用心设计游戏提供给玩家体验的一些细节元素。”宫崎英高解释，“通过这种层层递进的游戏开发流程，中间部分几乎只剩下一个目标，那就是补全游戏体验。”
2011年9月，《黑暗之魂》自发售后广受好评，主机版在Metacritic网站拿下89分的媒体均分。同年年底，《黑暗之魂》还在各种活动中斩获了大量奖项。FromSoftware在2014年《黑暗之魂3》发售前曾宣布，初代《黑暗之魂》的全球销量已超过200万份……如今，《黑暗之魂》被誉为历史上最具影响力的游戏作品之一，并凭借对《恶魔之魂》玩法模式的完善而备受推崇。
http://img.chuapp.com/wp-content/Picture/2026-10-20/7976ad73b278be39.jpg?imageView2/2/w/700
■ 血脉相连
在FromSoftware，宫崎英高几乎总是以总监身份带队开发游戏，但除了把控项目的整体方向之外，他还会深度参与关卡设计。即便在2014年升任FromSoftware社长后，宫崎英高仍然坚持这么做。
“高层次概念可能很容易想象，但我也会挑选一些亲自监督的细节，关卡设计就是其中之一。”宫崎英高说，“我认为在很大程度上，关卡决定了游戏带给玩家的基本感受和体验。我经常查看团队创作的关卡内容，并从中选出想要亲自监督设计的部分，因为我知道哪些环节对玩家体验的影响最大，以及在哪些地方可以将高层次概念与玩家看到的细节结合起来。”
虽然《黑暗之魂2》（2014年）不再由宫崎英高担任总监，但他仍然以监修角色参与了那款续作的开发。与初代作品相比，《黑暗之魂2》的预算和开发技术都有大幅提升，不过，两位联合总监涩谷知广和谷村唯并不想改变前作的既有模式或操作方式，而是深入挖掘了其备受玩家喜爱的原因。他们的努力收获了回报：《黑暗之魂2》的M站媒体均分达到91分，并且在发售后的短短1年内销量就超过了初代《黑暗之魂》。
http://img.chuapp.com/wp-content/Picture/2026-10-20/5186ad73bd4677a0.jpg?imageView2/2/w/700
从《黑暗之魂》《黑暗之魂2》的销量和口碑来看，黑魂系列的未来似乎一片光明，但为了潜心研究类魂品类接下来的进化方向，宫崎英高却决定暂时离开该系列，操刀开发一款全新IP游戏，即FromSoftware与索尼合作的《血源诅咒》。2015年3月，在《黑暗之魂2》问世仅一年后，这款PS4独占游戏正式发售。
《血源诅咒》借鉴了《黑暗之魂》的大量元素，包括高难度的第三人称动作战斗、RPG风格的角色成长系统、篝火式的提灯存档点，以及考验玩家技术的Boss战等等。与黑魂系列类似，《血源诅咒》融合黑暗奇幻、洛氏恐怖和哥特风格，并采用了甚至比《黑暗之魂》更抽象的叙事手法来展现其丰富的世界观。此外，《血源诅咒》还引入了更快的战斗节奏，这一点引起了许多玩家的共鸣。
按照宫崎英高的说法，在他的职业生涯中，《血源诅咒》是一部非常特别的作品。“首先，从工作室的角度来讲，我们在《血源诅咒》开发期间遇到了太多挑战，克服重重困难才完成了这款游戏。”宫崎英高指出，“另一个更重要的原因或许是，《血源诅咒》对我而言意义非凡，因为从剧情创作、世界观构建，到游戏机制和玩法系统的设计，我把自己的很多想法融入了游戏。因此，《血源诅咒》很可能是最能体现我个人风格的一部作品。”
http://img.chuapp.com/wp-content/Picture/2026-10-20/4706ad73c5d5f40a.jpg?imageView2/2/w/700
作为一款PS4独占游戏，《血源诅咒》无法触达Xbox和PC玩家，销量却超过了跨平台发行的黑魂系列前两代作品。在Metacritic网站上，《血源诅咒》的媒体均分高达92分，至今仍然被广泛视为2010年代最伟大的游戏之一。

完成《血源诅咒》的开发后，宫崎英高回到黑魂系列，担任《黑暗之魂3》联合总监，与另外两位总监涩谷知广、谷村唯共同为该项目掌舵。《黑暗之魂3》在玩法方面融合了黑魂系列和《血源诅咒》的精髓，并借鉴《血源诅咒》的快节奏战斗和叙事方式，延续了FromSoftware作品一贯的高品质。在许多玩家心中，《黑暗之魂3》是黑魂系列的集大成之作……2024年3月，发行商万代南梦宫宣布，“黑暗之魂”系列三部曲的全球销量已经超过3700万份。
在游戏行业，《恶魔之魂》和黑魂系列催生了“类魂”这一术语，后者常被用于描述遵循FromSoftware通过《恶魔之魂》《黑暗之魂》《血源诅咒》所确立的核心理念的游戏。许多从业者、媒体记者和玩家之所以将“类魂”挂在嘴边，是因为在过去的十几年里，市场上涌现出了大量深受宫崎英高作品启发的游戏。
http://img.chuapp.com/wp-content/Picture/2026-10-20/2116ad73c66e0d28.jpg?imageView2/2/w/700
■ 引领潮流
受FromSoftware旗下作品持续成功的启发，许多开发者纷纷制作与它们类似的游戏。随着时间推移，更注重技巧和策略的“类魂”游戏逐渐替代了本世纪初那些风格酷炫、以连击为特色的砍杀游戏，成为了动作游戏领域最主流的细分品类之一。
例如，日本厂商光荣特库摩的内部工作室Team Ninja以擅长开发风格独特且极具挑战性的动作游戏而闻名，曾经打造高难度动作游戏系列“忍者龙剑传”，但通过开发全新IP游戏《仁王》，Team Ninja成功借鉴了FromSoftware标志性的设计风格。
“坦白讲，我们之所以决定开发和发行《仁王》，《黑暗之魂》《血源诅咒》的商业和口碑成功是主要原因之一。”Team Ninja工作室负责人安田文彦承认，“《仁王》的立项很早（2004年），但开发工作曾数次被中断。2014年，当我们重启这个项目时，包括我在内，初始团队的几乎所有成员都已经是《恶魔之魂》《黑暗之魂》的忠实玩家。因此，我们深受那些游戏启发，决定再次打造一款能够直接吸引核心玩家的游戏。”
http://img.chuapp.com/wp-content/Picture/2026-10-20/8416ad73c794d6b5.jpg?imageView2/2/w/700
经过数年开发，初代《仁王》于2017年2月问世，并迅速收获了游戏媒体和玩家的广泛好评。随后几年间，光荣特库摩又推出了《仁王2》和《仁王3》。除了“仁王”系列之外，Team Ninja近年来还开发了《卧龙：苍天陨落》，对类魂品类进行了进一步探索。

Team Ninja并非唯一一家直接从宫崎英高作品中汲取灵感的工作室。与《仁王》一样，德国工作室Deck13开发、波兰厂商CI Games在2014年发行的《堕落之主》也明显受到了《黑暗之魂》启发。2023年，当《堕落之主》重启版发售时，CI Games高管更加明确地表示，黑魂系列是开发团队的重要灵感来源。“我认为《堕落之主》开发团队的部分任务，就是尝试构思《黑暗之魂3.5》。这是整个团队努力的方向和目标，我们从不掩饰。”CI Games创意产品组合策略师大卫·瓦贾洛（David Valjalo）说。

2023年9月，韩国厂商Neowiz推出了一款由旗下工作室Round8打造，美术风格和整体氛围与《血源诅咒》非常相似的类魂动作游戏：《匹诺曹的谎言》。该作改编自1883年出版的经典儿童文学作品《木偶奇遇记》，开发团队忠实地将FromSoftware的核心设计理念融入了游戏。《匹诺曹的谎言》总监崔智源坦称，Neowiz之所以立项开发这款与宫崎英高作品风格接近的游戏，很大程度上是因为类魂品类人气火爆，并且具备极大的商业潜力。此外，崔智源对类魂品类现状的研究，以及Round8在动作、近战格斗设计等方面的深厚造诣，也促成了《匹诺曹的谎言》的诞生。
http://img.chuapp.com/wp-content/Picture/2026-10-20/6356ad73c8551924.jpg?imageView2/2/w/700
“我想要接受挑战，制作一款全新的类魂游戏。”崔智源说，“虽然类魂品类很受欢迎，但与其他品类相比，除了FromSoftware和极少数几家其他工作室的作品之外，取得显著商业成功的类魂游戏仍然寥寥无几。这表明对开发团队来说，打造高质量的类魂游戏绝非易事，整个过程充满了挑战。与此同时，这种现状也激励着我们与同行竞争，努力推出一款比市场上已有产品更棒的类魂游戏。”

并非所有类魂游戏都满足于直接模仿FromSoftware作品的标志性元素。某些开发团队保留了类魂游戏的核心玩法，但会在游戏题材、美术风格和整体氛围等方面寻求创新。例如，《蟹蟹寻宝奇遇》是一款轻松诙谐的海底世界主题类魂游戏，兼具挑战性和幽默感，讲述了一只因欠税而被剥夺螺壳的寄居蟹的故事。对于《蟹蟹寻宝奇遇》，研发工作室Aggro Crab的创作初衷就是在保留类魂游戏整体框架的基础上，对该品类的经典元素进行创新。

“很多开发者被‘类魂游戏’的定义束缚，陷入了不断复制《黑暗之魂》的怪圈。在我看来，最好的魂游早已问世，它就是《黑暗之魂》。”Aggro Crab创意总监凯兰·波洛克（Caelan Pollock）解释，“《黑暗之魂》并不完美，但这恰恰是它能够引发玩家广泛共鸣，并对游戏行业产生深远影响的原因。我认为，如果开发者试图在方方面面模仿《黑暗之魂》，最终完成的游戏可能特别平庸，根本不值得玩家关注……我们之所以决定做出一些改变，既是为了推动游戏吸引更多玩家，也因为我们坚信，类魂品类仍有创新空间。我们赌了一把，赌的是玩家愿意接受与FromSoftware作品不太一样的类魂游戏。”
除了3D动作游戏之外，一些2D游戏也受到了类魂品类的影响，例如《盐与避难所》《重生细胞》和“渎神”系列等。
http://img.chuapp.com/wp-content/Picture/2026-10-20/6426ad73c920cc9e.jpg?imageView2/2/w/700

“初代《渎神》开发期间，我们深受魂系游戏的启发，但在战斗设计的某些方面并不想走魂游的老路。对我们来说，如何做取舍确实是个难题。”《渎神》设计师兼编剧迈克尔·奥尔特加（Maikel Ortega）透露，“我们最终决定保留类魂游戏中主角移动或战斗时的迟钝感，却不对角色施加任何实际的耐力限制。更重要的是，我们还保留了类魂游戏独特的探索感：游戏里没有任何明确路线，因为玩家探索的动力完全来源于好奇心。这正是我们的核心设计原则之一。”

items.title: 《Helldivers 2》工作室警告模组可能会因改用新的反作弊功能而崩溃，而 Steam 上的负面评论也像《地狱炸弹》一样不断下降
items.summary: Arrowhead says Easy Anti-Cheat will be more effective in combatting recent cheat mods, but the change has resu

content.v: Heads up, Helldivers: Arrowhead Game Studios is moving Helldivers 2 from GameGuard to Easy Anti-Cheat today, and that means some mods—including those that don't have any impact on gameplay—may stop working.

Helldivers 2 doesn't have official modding support, but there are plenty of them out there —most either cosmetic or audio replacements. Arrowhead said in a Steam update that while it hasn't previously taken a position on mods beyond warning that it can't guarantee their safety or usability, it's seen a recent uptick in cheat mods and it can't let that stand.

"We know mods are part of the DNA of PC gaming and gaming communities as a whole," the studio wrote. "In general, we appreciate the creativity behind cosmetic and non-gameplay mods, which players can enjoy without negatively impacting those who play alongside them.
"Where we need to improve is how we protect players against modifications that create unfair advantages or negatively impact others, which goes beyond software manipulation to tamper with our game."
Thus, two changes are being made:

Arrowhead said it's moving to Easy Anti-Cheat because GameGuard "wasn't as effective as it could have been," while EAC is more of an industry standard that should better protect the game. Unfortunately (although also appropriately, given the Helldivers context), there could be some collateral damage in the form of cosmetic mods, some of which may be caught up in the anti-cheat dragnet.

Because mod use in Helldivers 2 "is done at your own discretion," Arrowhead has no advice for what will or won't work, but it invited players to reach out to its support channel on Zendesk if they run into problems they believe are being caused by EAC. The only real fix, though, is to wait for mod makers to update their work.

As you might have anticipated, the move to EAC and its potential impact on mods has not gone over well with the Helldivers community: Since the announcement went up earlier today, more than 1,500 replies have been posted to the Steam discussion thread, and the traditional bombing of the reviews is also underway: 846 negative user reviews have been posted today alone, compared to just 146 positive.

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/cAxkd6D8y5iwfd6VRevWaB.png
Fields of Aaru

Release date : TBA I wasn't keen on the visual style of this ancient Egyptian afterlife farm sim based on its trailers but the low framerate animation and the soft, cohesive environment lighting actually really charmed me once I was hands-on with the demo. The characters have a lot of personality right off the bat and managing hydration to explore the desert is neat too. I also enjoy how, like Roots of Pacha, this one goes for a more abstract currency (memories) and daily objectives instead of high key capitalism.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/kBLi5Vr3M7LD5ELP49rBxc.png
Farm & Feast

Release date : November 11 I think this cute farming-plus-restaurant sim may click with me the way Travellers Rest didn't. The serving is actually pretty detailed, with making substitutions to menu items on each order, serving drinks, and typing receipt totals into a handset.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/RWxaJLuoDzwisB54QsE5Hk.png
Logisticats

Release date : TBA I really enjoy a chill city builder, but none have grabbed me since Fabledom. Logisticats seems like a real contender though, hitting that same intersection of semi-deep resource management with cute characters.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/aLvQG35UhweQvXZFfFzXkR.png
Beastfolk Barber

Release date : TBA Think Coffee Talk, but haircuts. It's mostly a visual novel with some hair styling minigames and a "gaining regulars to fulfill a demon bargain" plot. https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ZBhnonHpEvwZKWDgRurZ2e.png
Apple Crumble

Release date : December 3 I always want to get a little cozy horror into the mix and this weird thriller about a dramatic family gathering where someone's got it out for grandma on her 84th birthday looks like a gem. The full game is planned to only be about 60-90 minutes, the devs say, which is exactly the kind of snack-sized horror story I want.

items.title: 粉丝使用 AI 修复《遗落战境》重制版 PC 性能
items.summary: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered was excellent when it came out, bringing the beloved RPG to the mode

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2025/04/25/oblivion-remastered-op-ed-blogroll-1745589159142.jpg

The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered was excellent when it came out, bringing the beloved RPG to the modern era, but just like many other games running on Unreal 5, it was a technical mess. However, a fan has used Claude to create a performance mod that improves the game's performance.

When The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered came out back in April 2025, it was absolutely plagued with performance issues – something that's unfortunately become pretty normal these days. But, more than a year after launch, the performance issues are still there, with patch 1.2, the most recent on Steam, coming out all the way back in June 2025. And even after that patch, there were still significant performance problems.

It's little wonder, then, that the community would try to take matters into their own hands. Reddit user LTSharp posted on the ChatGPT subreddit , with a video showing the unpatched game running side-by-side with their patched version. And, while the raw increase to the frame rate isn't huge, LTSharp's patch greatly reduces the stutter, going from 66 hitches in the unpatched clip to just 11 in the patched version of the game.

In their post, LTSharp says one of the reasons for the rocky frametimes was that "the game was reconstructing the whole lighting of a scene in each frame even when nothing was changing, which was obviously a huge strain on CPU that had to parse all this work on a single thread."

They then ran Claude Opus 5.5 alongside Oblivion Remastered and tasked it with identifying the problems, and after two weeks, ended up with a patch. Crucially, this mod wasn't created by just entering a quick prompt into Claude, hitting enter, and then calling it a day. LTSharp describes the process as "two weeks of intense work" with a lot of trial and error involved.

It seems like the biggest source of the improved performance is spreading the work to more CPU cores. At any given moment in LTSharp's video, CPU utilization jumps from 35-40% to 50-60% utilization, with around two extra threads (workers) engaged. And given that these samples were recorded on a rig with a 5800X, there's probably some more room for improvement there.

AI usage is one of the biggest controversies in gaming right now, but this seems to be a decent use of the technology. This was just a person who was disappointed that after "upgrading from 2070 Super to 9070 XT, the game continued to run poorly, with low fps and stuttering," and decided to use Claude to fix the problem, despite not having any background in software development. Luckily, they've posted their work on GitHub, and if someone who's relatively inexperienced was able to reduce stutters by this much, I imagine there may be developers who can create forks of this project that might be able to eliminate them altogether.

This project is in contrast to some of the most egregious uses of the technology recently, like Epic, which recently delayed a Star Wars shooter to implement an AI-first policy where 'no hand-written code' is allowed. Likewise, an Xbox Business Analyst recently went on Twitter and ranted about how the game industry is 'pretending' to not use AI, and even made bold claims like, "If you're a game developer refusing to believe that AI has a place in your future, you should not be in the business of being a business."

items.title: Xbox Series X|S Is Getting A Surprise Graphics Boost From AMD
items.summary: Sony isn't the only company introducing new upscaling technology to its flagship PlayStation 5, as Microsoft a

content.v: Sony isn't the only company introducing new upscaling technology to its flagship PlayStation 5, as Microsoft and AMD have announced that FSR 4.1 is coming to more devices--including Xbox Series X|S consoles--in the future.

Similar to Sony's hardware-accelerated upscaling solutions for PS5 and PS5 Pro, AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) 4.1 is an advanced, machine-learning-based temporal image upscaling and reconstruction technology that can render a game at a lower resolution and then upscale it to a higher resolution.

While it's highly doubtful that Xbox Series X|S consoles will start offering PS5 Pro-like graphics (both consoles lack dedicated hardware for machine-learning algorithms), this should still give owners a noticeable bump in graphical quality and performance if implemented properly.

"At Xbox, we're building a gaming platform designed to meet players where they are and make it easier for creators to reach them," Xbox chief technology officer Scott Van Vliet said in the announcement video. "AMD has been an important partner in that journey for more than two decades. Together, our teams have been pushing gaming forward, across Xbox and Windows, from the silicon at the heart of our consoles and handhelds to technologies like DirectX, Advanced Shader Delivery, and Auto SR that help developers get more from the hardware and deliver better experiences for our players. Today, we're excited to take another step forward together, with FSR 4.1 coming to Xbox."
Van Vliet added that FSR 4.1 will come to Xbox Series X|S "soon," and that Microsoft and AMD are working to bring the tech to the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix .

Beyond that, AMD didn't share any more details on FSR 4.1 for Xbox Series X|S. FSR 1 and FSR 2 relied primarily on spatial algorithms or basic temporal accumulation to upscale games, and questions remain about who will adopt the technology and add support.

Just because the latest version of FSR is out doesn't mean a game will automatically use it. For example, Capcom built the console versions of Pragmata around FSR 1, scaling up from 720p on Xbox Series S and 1080p on Xbox Series X. FSR integration requires manual developer work and testing, so results may vary. We're already seeing signs of this on PS5 with Quick Spectral Super Resolution ; for now, only Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei will support the new AI upscaling upgrade on base PS5 consoles.

Essentially, developers will have to actually patch their games to use it; AMD FSR 4.1 will not automatically upgrade every older game overnight. The announcement comes just weeks before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 , and while Rockstar hasn't confirmed if its open-world game will utilize any upscaling technology like PSSR, QSSR, FSR 4.1, we could be looking at a current-gen arms race to find the best console to play the biggest game of the year on.

Beyond Xbox hardware, AMD FSR 4.1 will also be supported in Radeon RX 6000-series graphics cards, Gorgon Halo and Strix Halo Ryzen 9 laptops, and mobile gaming PC handhelds like the Asus ROG Xbox Ally devices that use Z2 Extreme and Z2A chipsets.

items.title: Palworld 粉丝在新民意调查中选出他们最喜欢的朋友，冬季更新被嘲笑
items.summary: Sekhmet is Palworld's homecoming queen, according to a new poll published by creator Pocketpair. The kitty-sha

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2024/01/25/palworldearlyaccessreleasedatetrailer-ign-blogroll-1704822459672-1706155084682.jpg

Sekhmet is Palworld 's homecoming queen, according to a new poll published by creator Pocketpair. The kitty-shaped Pal was voted the most popular by global players, scoring 49,637 votes. Solenne came in second with 37,425 votes, and Chillet was third with 34,625 votes. Spare a thought for little old Verdash, who, despite a green bouffant that would make any '90s emo kid proud, was at the bottom of the rankings with 1,479 votes.

Alongside the results, Pocketpair also teased a new update for this winter , Palworld: Side by Side. When I say "teased," I mean gave us three human silhouettes, sending the fandom into speculation mode about who the hidden characters could be. The prevailing Reddit theories are that the mystery figures are Auri, Zoe, and Saya, which would make sense, given that they were the top picks for most popular characters in the character rankings in the Pocketpair poll. All three are already in-game as faction leaders, or tower bosses, and given that Pocketpair made Zoe a recruitable companion after last year’s poll, it could mean that Side by Side will let players team up with the trio.

In an interview with Gaming World Interviews at Gamescom in August, Pocketpair head of publishing and communications John “Bucky” Buckley teased that Palworld’s next update would include something fans have been asking for. Pocketpair hasn’t confirmed whether that’s Side by Side. He also suggested the update’s timing was chosen to steer clear of November, presumably to avoid GTA 6’s release.

“It’s exciting for us at Pocketpair because we’re doing something that people have wanted for a long time,” he said. “We kind of considered it for 1.0, but it would have just pushed the release back too far. And, you know, not to be cliché, everyone’s saying it, but this year... something’s happening later [in the year]... So we didn’t want to go anywhere near the November kind of range.
“We’re doing something that’s really exciting, but it’s not big... We’re going to start the marketing on this soon. It’s not a huge thing. You don’t have to restart your game to experience it.”
If you're planning on heading back to the Palpagos Islands, take a look at all the new Pals added in Palworld 1.0 , plus a guide to all the Palworld bosses , and our interactive Palworld map .

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/10/rdr2-1789077021807.jpg
A bunch of games, including GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, are about to be pulled from the PlayStation Plus' catalog.

Next month, players will be losing some games that have been included with their PlayStation Plus Extra or Premium subscription. These are games that are currently available through Sony's Game Pass-like catalog of titles, so you're not being stripped of any games you own or are entitled to. However, if you've been waiting to play GTA 5 or Red Dead Redemption 2, you should move quickly, as those games amongst others will be removed from the service starting on November 17.
You can view the full list of games being removed below.
Games Being Removed from PS Plus Extra and Premium

Of course, GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 are being removed just two days before the launch of GTA 6. This is as good a time as any to catch up or revisit these titles if you're trying to build some extra hype for Rockstar's latest game. If you're not interested in an open world experience, The Talos Principle 2 is a fantastic first-person puzzle title that is absolutely worth playing before it leaves the service.

If you don't manage to play these games by November 17, they will become unplayable, even if they are downloaded to your machine, unless you purchase them. So, act quickly! If you do miss these titles, PlayStation recently added a bunch of other great games available through the service , including Mafia: The Old Country and Horizon Forbidden West.

items.title: “有一段时间没有玩过你的游戏机了吗？” Xbox 告诉客户库存短缺，以旧换新
items.summary: Xbox is sending emails to customers reminding them that they can trade in their Series X and S consoles if the

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2022/11/23/xboxseriesx-3-blogroll-1648735732292-1669247511678.jpeg

Xbox is sending emails to customers reminding them that they can trade in their Series X and S consoles if they’ve been collecting dust. The email has reportedly been sent to customers in the U.S. who haven’t used their console in some time.

The past year or so has seen console prices skyrocket thanks to the 'RAMpocalypse' sparked by generative AI companies such as OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Microsoft itself gobbling up components. As these AI companies vie for dominance and hoard all the RAM, prices soar for the end user while hardware is harder than ever to get hold of.

Valve’s Steam Frame VR machine was originally supposed to launch for $750 , for example, but thanks to the crisis created by AI companies, it ended up costing over $1,000. Meanwhile Nvidia graphics cards are way more expensive than they used to be.

Console price rises and shortages come at the worst time for both Sony and Microsoft, with November's launch of GTA 6 expected to spark a surge of interest in all things gaming. Given the game launches on console only, Rockstar's epic is sure to lead to a dramatic rise in PS5 and Xbox Series X and S sales. The only problem is, will Sony and Microsoft be able to meet demand?
With this in mind, you can see why Xbox would want people to hand over dormant consoles to new players. Here's what the email, verified by Windows Central , says:
“Haven’t played on your console in a while? If you’ve moved on to Xbox on PC or another way to play Xbox games, it may be time to trade in your console to Best Buy.”

This initiative was actually announced in June , when Microsoft said these consoles would be refurbished and resold at lower prices to make machines more readily available for customers. "We are working with retail partners on new programs to provide previously played consoles at lower prices," Microsoft said at the time. "Players who are ready to upgrade or no longer use their console will be able to trade it in with participating retail partners for cash or store credit. Those consoles will then be made available at lower prices for players."

The console hardware situation looks like it will get worse before it gets better. RAM manufacturers have reportedly sold their allocated memory capacity for 2027 already. The highest-end GPUs are near-impossible to get hold of unless you're willing to pay exorbitant amounts to a third-party seller.

items.title: 《ReBlade：死亡螺旋》首个预览 – 应对赛博朋克 Roguelite 游戏
items.summary: With an eye-catching setting and seriously satisfying combat and parry action, developer ChillyRoom's cyberpun

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/20/reblade-preview-blogroll-1792515184243.jpg
Key Preview Takeaways:

No other gameplay maneuver has had as much impact on modern action games as the parry. This ultimate skill suits both aggressive and defensive playstyles, letting you stylishly tip the scales of battle unscathed. Games like Sekiro, Lies of P, and the recent Onimusha: Way of the Sword lean into that focused combat style action fans have embraced. The upcoming ReBlade: The Death Spiral looks set to join that growing catalog of top-level action games that give you the tools and the satisfaction of tearing through enemies' defenses – this time within the framework of a roguelite.

Developer ChillyRoom has created a blend of a dungeon-crawling roguelite and fast-paced action-brawler, which leans into the idea of a cunning cybernetic warrior slashing and parrying through an ever-changing setting. In our hands-on with the ReBlade: The Death Spiral demo, we got to play over two hours of varied runs. This early hands-on made for a compelling onboarding experience for a stylish isometric roguelite action game, but we hope the full game shows much more of its core strengths in action.
Chinese Mythology by way of Cyberpunk

ReBlade: The Death Spiral's core concept centers on the steady exploration of a far-future megacity steeped in the mystique of Chinese mythology. Set in a sprawling metropolis ruled by cyborg gangs and warlords reimagined as deities and mythological figures, you play a nameless android who crawls out of the trash heap, damaged but still ready for a fight. They soon chart a path of destruction across the ruthless neon city, aiming to stop the cycle of violence and uncover the truth of their origins.

The concept feels like a mix of Alita: Battle Angel and Cyberpunk 2077, offering a visually stylized, brutal world to cut a path through. It has all the trappings of a dystopian sci-fi thriller, making a solid and infrequently seen framework for a roguelite brawler. It focuses on the protagonist as they cut their path through the procedurally generated upper layers of the metropolis. Along the way, she'll collect new weapons with slick abilities like chain lightning and fire-burst damage, plus new chip modifiers that further buff her stats. She can even use her heightened cyborg strength to pull off cool finishers and kick bombs back at vulnerable foes.

All the familiar elements of an action-RPG roguelite are here, but the cyberpunk-style and setting, plus the focus on fast, parry-heavy brawler action gives ReBlade a different flavor and perspective than its contemporaries. However, the overall narrative, at least as far as I can tell from this demonstration, is fairly light. It mostly relies on vibes and environmental storytelling to sell the setting and the protagonist's motivations. That's not necessarily a major negative, and the visual style and tone certainly helps ground ReBlade. However, after several runs, it still left me wanting more context and reasons to invest in the journey.
Cyber-City Dungeon Crawl

ReBlade really puts its weight on the core action of its many runs. Starting in the lower rungs of the megacity, you fight everything from lowly machine drones to hulking bruisers lurking on different floors. The action flows akin to other isometric top-down action-brawlers like Hades, and it does a good job of conveying the fast pace of combat. Using combo attacks, sub-weapon skills, buffs, and that all-important parry, I cut my way past enemy defenses. Landing a series of deflects is very satisfying, and it's especially cool to rapidly deflect enemy blaster shots back at surrounding enemies. Seriously, it felt immensely fun to pull off lightning-fast parries like this one during my different runs.

Even with the low-level gear you’re issued with at the start, ReBlade's combat fundamentals really do give you a sense of style and mastery when fighting enemies. I mostly stuck with the standard sword, which offers a balance of speed and power that I tend to favor, but I also had fun with the speedy twin blades and the heavier axe-and-shield combo. The action is further heightened by the more advanced weapons you'll find in dungeons and at various shops along the way. You can even swap certain buffs and perks between your gear to improve a favorite weapon found during a run. Tapping further into the cyberpunk angle, your protagonist can also augment themselves with different chips which add special modifiers to attacks, such as amplifying elemental damage or boosting recovery.

In an interesting change of pace from more linear roguelites, ReBlade lets you choose which path you want to take through its world. For each layer of the city, you're given choices about which areas to hit up, most of which are only available for a limited time before they disappear. This progression style let me focus on which weapon or performance upgrades and resource-gathering stages I wanted to pursue first. I really appreciated having a bit of choice in what loot I wanted, especially when I needed to save up cash before heading to one of the few shops that appear on the map.

ReBlade's combat really kicks into high gear during the boss encounters, which put the offense and defensive skills you've cultivated throughout a run to the test. These bosses blend cybernetic warlords and Chinese mythology, making the battles feel like the game is walking a fine line between a high-fantasy martial arts epic and a hard sci-fi action movie. I was really impressed by each boss's look and the design surrounding each battle; it delivered a showstopping finish to each layer. My favorite was a mysterious, wraith-like cyborg known as The Black, who fought like a cyber-enhanced grim reaper.

While I enjoyed ReBlade's spectacle and fast action, I found the demo sometimes felt a bit too generous. I didn't have much trouble getting through the two layers, especially when I found some great weapons that helped me clear enemies quickly. Moreover, you're also given a set of extra lives to help with runbacks on tougher challenges – which is very rare to see in a roguelite. While I like the ReBlade's focus on core action, I still felt some aspects of the roguelite structure were a bit underbaked and not fully realized as of this time, at least in this section of the game.

Still, this early demo offered some slick fights to dive into. With an eye-catching setting and seriously satisfying combat and parry action, developer ChillyRoom's cyberpunk roguelite concept shows solid promise as an action-RPG. While I hope ReBlade: The Death Spiral showcases a much deeper side in the full game, this early demo gets its stylized, grim world off to a solid start, and it's already got me ready to deflect and whittle down the cyborg opposition.
While you're here, check out these recent previews of other big upcoming games we've checked out recently!
Alessandro Fillari is a longtime games media professional. Talk video games with him on BlueSky at @afillari.bsky.social .

items.title: 《守望先锋》总监讨论了国王大道为何如此具有标志性，但也承认“游戏中的每张地图都有投票权”
items.summary: What's the best map in Overwatch? And why is it King's Row?

content.v: After Team 4 added map voting to Overwatch one thing became crystal clear: everyone wants to say they're a free thinker who doesn't follow the crowd until King's Row turns up, and then it's a landslide.

King's Row is widely considered to be the best map in Overwatch, I certainly think so. It's one of the few maps that's fun to play on defense and attack, as it doesn't seem overly weighted to either side, at least not until the very end.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/2QutxU4Ad4pJWKkyfNgAu-1920-80.jpg

"There's high ground there, but there's not oppressive high ground," Aaron Keller, game director of Overwatch explained to me after I asked him what, in his mind, made this such an iconic map. "There's areas for a lot of different heroes to do their things. It's fairly tight and close, so you're not going to get out of the action for too long.

"Another thing that I think about a lot with King's Row—sorry this could go on for a really long time—I think that there's something about being able to play through most of the space in a map that I think is just more satisfying for both teams. It can feel really good to hold a team at spawn, but you don't want that every game. You want to feel like it's a close [game]."

As someone who mostly plays support heroes and has put a hell of a lot of time into Ana I can tell you that King's Row is my favourite map thanks to all of its clear sightlines and the fact that tanks never stray too far away from the payload, although the mid stretch can get a bit dicey at times. What I love the most, however, is how you're almost always coming face to face with the enemy providing "big team fight moments" the whole way through the map. But not everyone will agree with me.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/CAFbWN6bqsH97gKvX2yM74-1920-80.jpg

"I do think sometimes there can be a sort of agreement that happens as more people vote for King's Row," Keller says. "It just starts to get some momentum there." There are a good deal of people who either vote with what the group wants or just don't vote at all, but every so often players go against the grain.

"Every single map in the game gets a vote," Keller says. "For some people Clash or 2CP is their favourite mode in Overwatch. Even though we think that there's some issues with them, but I think the playerbase is more varied than we think sometimes." I don't doubt that some people love 2CP. Even I wouldn't say I minded it much, although its second objective had some serious issues, which was one of the reasons as to why it ended up getting pulled from the map rotation.

I'm not sure whether Team 4 has tried to recreate the magic that they captured with King's Row, although Neon Junction sort of feels like it but in reverse. But that's alright, because there's plenty of other good maps to be enjoyed, although I know where my voting allegiances lie.

items.title: 索尼老板：“创造力是人类的，而不是人工智能的”
items.summary: Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick and Sony Group President and CEO, Hiroki Totoki, commented on the future of gami

content.v: Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick and Sony's top boss, Hiroki Totoki, commented on the future of gaming today at the Paley International Summit. Naturally, the topic of AI came up, and Totoki believes AI technologies will not replace humans in game development, in part because of the creativity required.

"Creativity is for humans, not AI,” Totoki said, as reported by IGN . “How to use the technology profile is important. Of course, I encourage my people to use AI in a certain manner, but at [the] same time we try to keep the rights and rights holders and creators and artists.”
For his part, Zelnick said it's his belief that AI itself will not replace a developer, but instead, people who don't embrace AI might be replaced by people who do.

"I’m fond of saying AI is a collection of datasets, compute, and large language models. That’s what it is. And datasets, by definition, are backward-looking. That’s all they are. And creativity, at its best, is forward-looking," he said.

Zelnick said ideas that are "completely unexpected" don't come from algorithms--they come from creative people making surprising, original choices. To make his point, Zelnick said when he was an executive at Fox, he oversaw the release of Home Alone, a movie that no one expected to be a success.
"It turned out to be the highest-grossing comedy of all time. So if hits are unexpected, data sets aren’t gonna get you there, no matter how fluent they are," he said.

Both PlayStation and Take-Two have embraced AI, with PlayStation heavily leveraging the technology in its game-development processes . As for Take-Two, the publisher is utilizing the technology for its workflows , but there is no AI in GTA 6 .

There has been significant pushback for AI in game development from developers and players alike, with many expressing concerns about job security, legal issues, and simply the further "enshi**ification" of everything they love.

items.title: Switch 1 发布 10 年后，我还没在屋顶派对上玩过游戏
items.summary: It's now been a full decade since Nintendo announced the first Switch, which is almost hard to believe, given

content.v: It's now been a full decade since Nintendo announced the first Switch, which is almost hard to believe, given how fresh that reveal trailer still feels in our heads. Heaps of hype and a lack of information from Nintendo about its Wii U successor, codenamed "NX," led to the company's fanbase becoming increasingly restless.

Reports and rumors pointed to the NX as a console-handheld hybrid , but Nintendo didn't fully unveil the Switch until October 20, 2016 (an announcement preluded by a photo of Mario being a creep ). The three-and-a-half-minute video made it clear how Nintendo wanted players to interact with the Switch, showing several scenarios where people take their games on the go.

Rewatching that trailer today, it's amusing to look back at how Nintendo foresaw the social impact of the Switch. Some moments from the trailer manifested in reality, while others were hilariously exaggerated.

You have a guy taking his dog (and his copy of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild) out on a walk, a traveler playing Skyrim on a plane and putting the game on his television upon his arrival home, and professional Splatoon players practicing before their big moment on stage.

And then, there's "Nintendo Karen." The most-talked-about moment in the trailer centered on a woman playing Super Mario Odyssey before being prompted to join friends for a rooftop party (a typical gathering of millennials, as people would joke back then), during which she breaks out the Switch, pulls out that dinky little kickstand, and plays a game with a friend as onlookers holding red Solo cups watch with indifference. Fans branded this commercial character as "Karen" and debated the social implications of bringing a Switch to such a function.

The Nintendo Switch reveal trailer remains a striking piece of marketing, with its upbeat vibe and extra emphasis on the Switch's branding (much needed, after the Wii U's marketing failures). In the years since the Switch's release, I’ve seen Switches out in the wild, just as Nintendo imagined, though I've yet to go to a rooftop party like the one Karen attended.

While the Switch 2 continues to sell well, there's a notion that its reveal was a bit cold and lacking in fanfare compared to the original Switch. Even so, Nintendo still hasn't lost its charm and quirk, even though the company will probably never use that hilarious picture of Mario behind the curtain ever again.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass 的最新浪潮以大型最终幻想冒险为主角
items.summary: Right on schedule, the second wave of games coming to Xbox Game Pass has been revealed. After the first batch,

content.v: Right on schedule, the second wave of games coming to Xbox Game Pass has been revealed. After the first batch, which included Gears of War: E-Day, Battlefield 6, and more, the rest of the month will add games like Final Fantasy 7 Remake and The Seance of Blake Manor to the subscription service. We've also gotten a sneak peek at what's coming in November, so there's plenty to play over the next couple of weeks.
As a reminder, several games are also leaving Xbox Game Pass this month , including a pair of Double Fine classics and one massive Star Wars Lego game.

Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade is the headline act in this new wave of arrivals, right on time for anyone looking to experience the saga from its first chapter. The Intergrade version includes the original game and its Yuffie-centric expansion, but you'll have to wait until October 29 to embark on the Unknown Journey.

Before then, you can grab the Game Preview edition of Sandustry on PC starting October 21. A game about exploration and automation, it's a tempting download for anyone who enjoys assembly-line video games. You can also get Dodo Duckie on October 22, a reality-bending odyssey where you'll get to outsmart aliens and solve puzzles while wielding duck powers, and October 26 will see the MMO-lite action RPG Scramble Knights Online make its day-one debut on Game Pass.

The Séance of Blake Manor was one of GameSpot's favorite games of 2025 , and you can check out this supernatural detective mystery for yourself when it's added to the Game Pass library on October 27. Starting October 29, you can explore Midgar in the aforementioned Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade, play classic Plants vs. Zombies in HD, and the horror-parkour game Terrible Lizards is another day-one release to round out the month.
Looking ahead, November will kick off with Pit of Goblin, an online horror co-op adventure in which you play as a scrappy goblin.

items.title: 华硕 ProArt P16 (H7607) RTX Spark 笔记本电脑评测
items.summary: The best RTX Spark machine, but is it the best for you? Probably not…

content.v: If you don't talk to me about the price, I will tell you the Asus ProArt P16 is an unbelievably good gaming laptop. It is beautifully slim, runs incredibly well gaming on battery, and has an absolutely stunning 16-inch OLED screen. And its Arm-based SoC is almost entirely transparent when it comes to running pretty much anything on Windows 11.

But this is no mere Snapdragon device, this the RTX Spark ; Nvidia's first foray into the world of full Windows SoCs. It's pairing a relatively beefy RTX Blackwell GPU with a whole bunch of Arm CPU cores, and doing so with lots and lots and lots of LPDDR5X memory. Y'know, for AI.

Which, er, is why you might not want to ask about that price. Memory's expensive, and these RTX Spark laptops—of which the Asus ProArt P16 is, in my opinion, the most desirable—are likewise brutally priced. I have the 64 GB version, with the top Nvidia N1X SoC inside it, and it will set you back $4,400.

It is that price both for AI and because of AI, and is being sold as the 'One PC' that can do everything. It can game, it can run creative apps, and it can slam through local AI workloads like no other laptop before. But where you're probably expecting me to trot out the old 'jack of all trades, master of none' line here, that's not really the case. There are tradeoffs, sure, but it's really, really good at the lot. And did I mention it was pretty?

The real question here, however, is whether a PC gamer ought to be considering this machine for their next laptop. And if it's just to play games on, this would not be my first choice, however good a device I think it is. The performance, for an Arm-powered laptop, is impressive in terms of the experience, but not faultless. While Microsoft is working hard on Prism and opening up support for every anti-cheat software going, it is not complete. And checking against my back-of-the-napkin list of the 15 biggest PC games around right now you're looking at around half of them not being playable. Yet.
Buy if...
✅ You're a creator or local AI head who games on the side: If you're after an almost workstation style thin and light machine, but also want to play after dark, the ProArt P16 will cover all bases
Don't buy if...

❌ You just want a gaming laptop: There are other thin and light gaming machines that will cost a fraction of what this does, but perform as well in-game. ❌ You have to ask the price: These are machines for the very well-off PC user.
Asus ProArt P16 - Features
CPU
Nvidia RTX Spark N1X
Cores
20 total (10 Arm Cortex-X925 + 10 Arm Cortex-A725)
GPU
Nvidia Blackwell RTX
Cores
6144 CUDA cores

64 GB LPDDR5X RAM
Storage
1 TB NVMe M.2 SSD
Screen
16-inch 3K OLED 100% DCI-P3 120 Hz Touchscreen
OS
Microsoft Windows 11 Home 64-bit
Colour
Nano Black
Warranty
ASUS 12 Month Collect & Return Warranty
Price

There are many like it, but this one is mine: The 20-core N1X chip, with 10 performance and 10 efficient cores, and the 6144 CUDA core GPU component. This version also comes with a 1 TB SSD (for a $4,400 spec? 😬 I know) and 64 GB of LPDDR5X-9400 memory.

This version of the ProArt P16 is rocking the 16-inch 2880 x 1800 touchscreen OLED display, while there is also a 3840 x 2400 OLED screen available (both 120 Hz) if you go for one of the even pricier models. That one's a touch brighter, but this 1800p OLED will still output at 500 nits, with a 1100 nit peak HDR output, so it's no slouch.

The paucity of storage is a definite disappointment for something at this price—look lower down the stack and you'll still be paying $2800 for the 24 GB version with just a 512 GB SSD. And I honestly do not see the point in that one except for all concerned to be able to say RTX Spark laptops "start from $2800". There is, however, a spare PCIe Gen5 SSD slot in the rear of the machine, which is easily accessible once you remove lots of torx screws.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/v6MexP7DQk8scp2tmb6iPL-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/335dER7yYLxcPPfk7AdnLL-1920-80.jpg

The keyboard would be a genuinely lovely thing for this device if I wasn't regularly getting additional keystrokes I did not ask for. I've had to keep deleting the extra spaces this thing keeps adding into my copy. There. I just had to kill another one. It's annoying.

What isn't annoying at all, though, is the glorious, massive haptic touchpad Asus has jammed onto this thing. It quite literally takes up half the width of the device. It's great to the touch, and impressively responsive as your digits glide across its surface. Mmm. Smooth.

It's meant to have a webcam, too, but I cannot for the life of me find out how to turn the damned thing on. I'm assuming that somewhere in there a ribbon cable has become ejected because the device sees nothing. This is what I mean by some quality control issues...
Asus ProArt P16 - Value
Haha. Hahahahahaha. Hahahahahahahahahahahaha.
C'mon. This is the mid-range ProArt P16 for $4,400 . Any sense of value left the station a loooooooong time ago.
Asus ProArt P16 - Sound
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/YHyysLxiMW35yvZ4fZ9aVE-1920-80.jpg

This is a very pleasant surprise. The up-firing speakers set either side of the ProArt P16's keyboard are really, really good. Obviously that's still really, really good for laptop speakers, and they're are never going to replace your bookshelf speakers, but for clarity and, yes, even bass they do incredibly well.

And they're loud enough that they can largely overcome the sound coming out of the vents on the ProArt P16 when it's running in full performance mode. It does get rather chatty when the silicon is running at full throttle, and when you're talking about a system that's going to max out its GPU component when running both games and local large language models, that's probably going to happen quite a lot.

The pleasing thing, however, is that knocking things down to the Balanced preset in the ProArt Creator Hub (essentially a reskinned Armoury Crate) means that your performance only drops by a few percentage points but the fan noise drops by a whole hell of a lot. It's not silent—you have to dip into Whisper mode for that—but this is the preset you're going to want to spend most of your time running in.
Asus ProArt P16 - Performance
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/43r9NsyWuCiCCXfqYWp4eL-1920-80.jpg

Somewhat inevitably, performance is a mixed bag of chips when it comes to the RTX Spark. For one, this is a first-gen product from Nvidia, fusing essentially off-the-shelf Arm cores with its own GPU cores, so broad, mature support was never going to be 100% there from the get-go. For another we're talking about games especially that are being run through the Microsoft Prism emulation layer in order for them to run at all on the Asus ProArt P16.

But even taking all that into account I think the gaming performance of this device is pretty damned impressive. The general suggestion ahead of the launch was that the 6144 CUDA core version would deliver gaming performance at a similar level to the RTX 5070 mobile GPUs. It has more cores than the mobile silicon, but is running at a lower clock speed and with a lower power budget, too.

Take a look at the relative 1080p gaming performance of Cyberpunk 2077 and Metro Exodus Enhanced Ed. running on the RTX Spark versus the 100 W Framework 16 or 115 W Razer Blade 14 and you can see where it doesn't quite match up to the GPU performance of the more thirsty graphics parts.

items.title: DLSS Swapper 现在可以让您同时更新多个游戏中的所有升级程序，添加了 Nvidia 的新帧生成预设 C
items.summary: Everything, everywhere, all at once.

content.v: DLSS Swapper just became even more useful, as the upscaler-switching software has rolled out a bulk DLL swapping feature in the latest update.

Version 1.2.7.0 adds a Bulk Swap button to the top right hand menu. Click on it, and you can select multiple games (or all of them) from your libraries at once, before individually selecting your upscaling version preferences in one handy menu (via Techpowerup ). Hit apply, and they all get updated at the same time.

There are many different iterations of DLSS, FSR, and XeSS to choose from, including separate frame generation options and individual upscaler presets. And should a change cause issues, your games can be restored to their original DLLs and preset settings en masse, too.

It's the little things in life, isn't it? This update also adds DLSS Frame Generation Preset C , which is the new beta version that is supposed to significantly boost performance in exchange for a slight drop in visual fidelity. Up to 35% on an RTX 5060, supposedly.

I've had some odd visual results when messing around with different upscaler versions in certain games ( Crimson Desert , I'm looking at you), so the option to easily roll back changes either individually or all at once is a welcome one. I might have a mess around with Preset C later, though, just to see if I can gain a few frames.

A word of warning. DLSS Swapper points out on first boot that messing around with game files could cause some anti-cheat software to flag the changes, so it's probably best to avoid anything with an online component. Lest the banhammer strike for thee.
